description: The row-cap half of the new reporting rule names a condition the tool result never states: the prompt keys on a run_sql result saying the query stopped at the row limit, but the only cap text emitted is 'Result truncated at {cap_size} rows. Re-issue with an explicit LIMIT or narrower WHERE clause.'

The payload-failure WARNING 'table payload construction failed; serving Markdown only' no longer describes what the code does, since the payload is None path now emits a user-visible text block; the header-only-over-budget case logs nothing at all.

'each withheld table or text block logs INFO server-side' no longer holds for every withheld result: a schema-introspection DataFrame whose payload cannot be built takes the new payload is None branch, where the text block is suppressed and nothing is logged.

A row-cap hit with no max_rows attribute silently loses the user-facing cap notice: cap_size defaults to 0, row_cap_of rejects 0, so widget notice, Markdown cap sentence and CSV warning are dropped while the agent-facing note reads 'Result truncated at 0 rows', with no log of the discrepancy.

Stale prose around the table-payload fallback: the 'degrade to no widget and let the Markdown answer stand' comment and the 'serving Markdown only' WARNING, plus line 68's 'per-block cap above' now that _MAX_TABLE_PAYLOAD_BYTES moved to _table_payload.py.

row_cap_marker_data does not enforce the invariant row_cap_of requires: the constructor accepts any value int() can coerce, so a malformed marker is silently reinterpreted as 'no cap' at every read site.
'cap was hit' and 'cap value' are conflated into one optional row_cap int, so a hit with an unknown cap degrades silently to 'not capped' on every user surface.

The table block stays an anemic dict whose cross-field invariant is restated at four sites, and the widget revalidates row_cap while the Markdown path takes it on trust and feeds it to an f-string that raises on a non-numeric value.
The 'no row fits' case (row_count == 0, truncated >= 1) has no test for either new message, so the 'Showing the first 0 of 1 rows' wording and the agent's 'first 0 of them' line are unprotected.
The Markdown row_cap path has no type guard where row_cap_of and the widget both have one, and no Python test covers a malformed value, though the widget side has a parametrized test.

test_cut_result_rule_and_no_full_table_wording is brittle beyond the rule it protects: eight literal-substring assertions plus a loop forbidding 'the full ' anywhere in the prompt, including legitimate unrelated future wording.
_compute_table_payload now runs twice per query with no memoization, test or guard on the cost, doubling a full serialization plus binary search on the request path for large results.
The agent-facing cue in the new prompt rule paraphrases rather than quotes the literal strings a run_sql result carries, making the trigger less unambiguous than it could be.
AGENTS.md still enumerates the private top-level helpers without _table_payload.py and its architecture tree omits the new shared module this PR makes the single owner of table-payload sizing.

Every successful read query now serializes the table payload twice, once in run_sql_display_line and again in the formatter's _build_table_payload; the shared calculation could memoize on the component.

_render_dataframe hand-builds its block dict without a row_cap key, making it a second cap-blind payload builder, and _small_result_to_markdown's docstring does not mention the row-cap sentence the function now appends.
Single-row counts read ungrammatically in generated prose: 'this CSV holds only the 1 rows shown' and, symmetrically, 'The query returned 1 rows that could not be displayed.'
